findings.F1: The giveback lives almost entirely in up days that come after a 5-day fall. In folds B and C, in-profile up days whose prior 5-day return was in the lowest quartile (below -4.6 %) were followed by a short-side return of +1.82 % over the next day (t 3.23, 160 cases), +1.85 % over two days and +1.51 % over three days. Up days after a 5-day rise of +0.9 % to +8.8 % lost -0.63 % the next day (t -1.32) and -1.31 % over three days. All 637 cases together earned only +0.67 % next day, and their effect is gone by day 3 (-0.04 %).
findings.F2: The prior 5-day fall is not an effect of its own on the short side. In-profile down days with the same lowest-quartile 5-day return were followed by a short-side return of -1.13 % the next day (t -4.15, 382 days) and -1.42 % over three days. These coins rebound when there is no up day. The condition earns the short only together with the idea's rise, which fits the brief's theory: a squeeze up day inside a running decline is the overshoot that trapped holders sell into.
findings.F3: The book's deepest fall, -5.7 % in w14, and its worst days came on days when the coins rose strongly. Its worst days lost -5.2 %, -3.5 % and -2.1 % while the coins' mean return was +11.0 %, +5.9 % and +12.5 %. Across days, the book's mean return falls steadily from +0.14 % on the coins' worst-day quintile to -0.11 % on their best-day quintile. These losses on squeeze continuations are what hold the Calmar at 0.33.
findings.F4: The sizing puts its weight where the effect fails, and holding on costs money.
findings.F5: The effect points the same way in every year explored but is weak in 2020. Next-day short-side returns were +1.40 % (t 2.90) in 2018, +0.68 % in 2019, +0.14 % in 2020 and +0.65 % in 2021. The book earned +2.2 % a year against the coins' much larger swings, with nine of twelve windows within ±1.2 %.

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, a coin's one-day rise that comes after a fall over its last 5 days is followed by a fall over the next 3 days that grows with the size of the rise against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days and with the depth of that 5-day fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader in an agitated decline should short only the bounce that interrupts a fresh slide and hold it about three days, which spreads the fee over a larger move, and should not short bounces that extend a short-term rise.
ideas.name: Bounce inside fresh slide fades

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, a coin's one-day rise is followed by a larger fall over the next 1 day the deeper the coin's 5-day return before the rise, graded by the rise against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader should weight the next-day short of an agitated-decline bounce by how hard the coin fell in the days before it, rather than by the size of the bounce alone.
ideas.name: Post-slide bounce next-day giveback
